title: ImportWizard
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) holding a NavigationStack with MonarchStepper, then per step MonarchFileUpload (.fileImporter for .commaSeparatedText), MonarchColumnMapping, MonarchPreviewRows with ProgressView(.monarchLinear) while importing, and a result notice; a bottom bar of MonarchButton Back and Continue in .safeAreaInset; TabularData's DataFrame(contentsOfCSVFile:) reads the file
summary: A recipe, not a component: importing records from a CSV file in four steps in a sheet: choose the file, match its columns to fields, check the rows, then import and see what was saved.
whenToUse: When people bring a spreadsheet of records into the app, such as contacts, products or members, and need to match columns and see problems before anything is saved.
whenNotToUse: For attaching a file to a record use MonarchFileUpload alone. For a short task without a file use the wizard-dialog recipe. On iPad or Mac, where a wide table fits, the same steps can be pushed screens instead of a sheet.

states.name: upload
states.description: MonarchFileUpload limited to one CSV file; a file that cannot be read, or has no data rows, shows a danger MonarchInlineNotice and stays on this step.

states.name: map
states.description: MonarchColumnMapping pre-filled from MonarchColumnMapping.suggest; Check rows is disabled while a required field has no column.

states.name: preview
states.description: MonarchPreviewRows shows each row's status; rows with errors are skipped and the button reads "Import 2 rows". Nothing is saved yet.

states.name: importing
states.description: A linear ProgressView reads Importing 2 rows…, the import button shows its spinner, and Back and Cancel are disabled.

states.name: results
states.description: A success notice with what was created and skipped; Done closes the sheet.

states.name: started
states.description: After the first step the sheet cannot be swiped away; Cancel in the toolbar closes it.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with MonarchStepper, Monarch text styles, the mapping and preview components in their own theme colours, the Monarch linear progress style, and a bottom bar with a secondary Back and a primary next button.
platformNotes: The web ImportWizard is one component that parses the CSV itself, offers a template download and a downloadable problems CSV, validates rows through a callback, picks a duplicate rule and reports created, updated, skipped and failed counts. On iOS the app composes the steps: it reads the file with TabularData's DataFrame (or its own parser), validates rows into MonarchPreviewRow errors and warnings, and shows the report; a problems file can be offered with ShareLink, and a duplicate rule with a Picker on the preview step. The web shows the preview as a wide table; on iPhone MonarchPreviewRows lays rows out for the narrow screen. Android plans the same recipe. Status experimental: it is a product pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: MonarchStepper reads "Step 2 of 4" and each step's state; the step title has the header trait.
Post an AccessibilityNotification.Announcement of the new step when Continue or Back changes it, since focus stays on the button.
MonarchFileUpload, MonarchColumnMapping and MonarchPreviewRows keep their own labels, values and announcements.
The progress view is read with its title and percentage; failures are text with an icon, not colour alone.
Cancel is in the toolbar with the cancellation placement, so it remains once swiping the sheet away is disabled.
edgeCases: A file with only a header row, or without column names, stays on the upload step with a message.
Duplicate header names: give the later ones a suffix before building the mapping sources.
Very large files: read and validate off the main actor and show the first rows in the preview; MonarchPreviewRows pages its rows.
When no row can be imported, disable the import button and say why.
Reset every step's state when the sheet is presented again.

examples.title: Contacts import

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws the four steps as a row with each name beside its circle, which needs about 420 points; a phone column has 306, so the stepper shows its compact form (Step 1 of 4, the name of the step and a progress bar). The page, the file drop area, the template link and the buttons are inline, as on the web.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: progress through steps at compact width is a summary, not a row of names
